subject: Workplace Skills
title: Champions Drive Adoption
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Champions Drive Adoption.

hook.text: Everett Rogers found that innovations spread through networks, not announcements. Adoption is social, not logical.

buildup.text: Early adopters try new things. Early majority waits for proof. Late majority needs social pressure. Laggards resist.

discovery.text: Champions are trusted peers who demonstrate the value of change. Their endorsement carries more weight than any memo.

twist.text: Executives often try to mandate adoption top-down. Peer influence is three times more effective at changing behavior.

climax.text: Find your champions early. Give them resources, visibility, and let them tell their story to the majority.

punchline.text: People follow peers, not memos. Find your champions.

quiz.question: Why are peer champions more effective than executive mandates?
options: Champions have more authority than executives
Peer influence is stronger than top-down mandates for behavior change
Champions work for free and save budget
